source_updates.Fact_A2: [A2] For $N\ge2$, the zero-FI correspondence supplier identifies the stable-and-costable real quotient with the framed ordinary ASD sector having $q_N=-k$, preserving the specified orientation, unitary framing, compact torus action and exact first-order family qualifications. For $N=1$, the rank-one boundary lemma proves that both ordinary spaces are empty at $k>0$ and are the framed flat point at $k=0$, with compatible compact actions and an explicit first-order groupoid equivalence. Its stabilization proof retains the rank-two supplier's actual GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites; it introduces no extra rank-one dictionary premise. The two suppliers therefore cover the ordinary dictionary for every $N\ge1$ at exactly those inherited holds. Neither identifies the positive-FI resolution or its rank-one formal coefficients with ordinary ASD moduli. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]], [[lem-qftx-rank-one-regular-adhm-and-ordinary-asd-boundary]]
source_updates.proof_step_2_2: 2.2 For $N\ge2$, the source and target of [A2]'s rank-two-and-higher supplier agree with the zero-FI regular quotient and the framed ASD sector in the conditional dictionary, with $q_N=-k$ and identical framing and orientation. For $N=1$, stabilize by adding one unused framed line as in the boundary lemma: its moment equations, word stability and costability are unchanged. Its proved boundary identifies the two empty spaces at $k>0$ and the unique framed flat points at $k=0$, and its direct first-order gauge argument supplies the corresponding family identification rather than inferring it from an orbit-set bijection. Thus the ordinary dictionary has no uncovered rank-one case; its genuine rank-two analytic and normal-form holds remain inherited. This does not place any positive-FI partition fixed point in the open regular ordinary locus. In particular, the positive-FI one-box rank-one contribution is still the formal coefficient of step 1.1 and is not an ordinary positive-charge abelian instanton. [given, A2, L2, step 1.1, algebra]

batch60_A_inventory_append.title: Rank-one regular zero-FI ADHM and ordinary ASD boundary
batch60_A_inventory_append.statement:
Assume AC and the exact rank-two regular zero-FI ADHM/ASD correspondence, with all its actual analytic and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites. Fix $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,1}$ be the orbit set by $U(V)$ of $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ with

$$[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad [B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0,$$

such that words in the $B_i$ applied to $I(W)$ span $V$ and no nonzero common invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$. On the positively stereographically oriented unit round $S^4$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,1}$ be the set of smooth Hermitian line bundles $L$, smooth unitary connections $A$ with $F_A^+=0$, and unitary framings $\Phi:L_\infty\to\mathbb C$, with $q_1=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int F_A\wedge F_A=-k$, modulo framed unitary isomorphisms. After a fixed framed bundle is chosen, its gauge group consists of smooth unitary automorphisms equal to identity at infinity.

The regular complex $GL(V)$ quotient, defined by retaining the complex equation and the same stability and costability, has the same empty-or-point classification under the zero-FI real/complex quotient identification. For $k>0$ both ordinary sets are empty. For $k=0$ they are the single empty raw datum and the framed flat line, respectively, with no framed stabilizer. This identification is equivariant for $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$, with $h=e^{-1}$, raw action $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$ and connection action by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing with $h$; on the resulting point these actions are trivial.

A first-order real Hermitian family here is over $D=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ with involution $\varepsilon^\dagger=\varepsilon$. On the raw side use free $D$-modules of ranks $k,1$, the displayed equations over $D$, regular reduction, fixed framing module, and unitary $D$-linear changes of basis. On the connection side use locally free smooth Hermitian line-bundle deformations with framed special fiber and a unitary connection $A_0+\varepsilon a$, satisfying ASD coefficientwise, modulo unitary gauge transformations with framed reduction and value identity at infinity. For $k>0$ these groupoids are empty; for $k=0$ each is equivalent to the one-object groupoid with trivial automorphism group. The identification commutes with reduction, infinitesimal scalar base changes preserving the involution, and the compact action. In particular it identifies their zero tangent spaces and restricts to the exact locally-free/base-change family range in the rank-two correspondence. No positive-FI quotient, its non-locally-free rank-one boundary, or its fixed-point series is identified with ordinary ASD moduli.

Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}$ be the quotient by $U(k)$ of the raw data satisfying both zero moment equations and stable-and-costable regularity in the conventions stated in the following references section. Let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ with $q_N=-k$ in those same conventions. Conditional on the real monad normalization and Ward inputs stated below, the construction gives a $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$-equivariant bijection

$$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}\;\longleftrightarrow\;\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}.$$

The zero-FI real quotient is also diffeomorphic to the stable-and-costable complex $GL(k)$ quotient. Under the stated projective GAGA and family base-change hypotheses, the corresponding framed sheaves on $\mathbb P^2$ are exactly the locally free locus among the framed torsion-free sheaves with rank $N$ and Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$. The positive-FI stable quotient includes non-locally-free sheaves and is not identified with the ordinary framed ASD moduli. Under the same family and normal-form hypotheses, the correspondence is compatible with first-order framed deformations and their tangent spaces.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.
Assume countable choice. For $n\ge1$, $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(S^n)$ is $\mathbb R$ in degrees $0,n$ and zero otherwise. For $S^0$ it is $\mathbb R^2$ in degree zero and zero otherwise.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be an oriented smooth $n$-manifold with boundary, $n\geq1$, and let $\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)$. With $j:\partial M\hookrightarrow M$ and the outward-normal-first orientation,
$$\int_M d\eta=\int_{\partial M}j^*\eta.$$
An empty boundary contributes zero; in dimension one its integral is a finite signed sum of point values.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

derivations.claim: Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient. [A1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

Independently, stabilize any framed unitary ASD line connection by the trivial framed flat line. The result is a smooth unitary ASD rank-two connection. Its determinant connection is the original line connection, since $\det(L\oplus\mathbb C)=L$ and the added connection is flat. By [F2] the original connection is flat, so $q_1=0$. Its sector is therefore empty if $k>0$. If $k=0$, transport the unit vector fixed by its framing from infinity. Any two paths differ by a null-homotopic loop by [F3]; subdivide a compact null-homotopy into finitely many cells lying in parallel-frame coordinate balls. Boundary transports in each cell are identity and internal edges cancel, so the loop transport is identity. The resulting global unit parallel section gives the unique framed isomorphism to the trivial flat line. A parallel automorphism fixing its value at infinity is identity. On the raw side at $k=0$ every map is the unique zero-dimensional map, both regularity conditions hold, and $U(0)$ is trivial. This proves the point classification and absence of framed stabilizers. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

To type first-order bundle families without presuming a global trivialization, first use step 1.2 to identify the special fiber with its framed parallel line. Choose local lifts of this frame in a locally free Hermitian $D$-line family. If a lift has Hermitian Gram scalar $1+\varepsilon r$ with $r$ real, multiplication by $1-\varepsilon r/2$ makes it unitary, so unitary local lifts exist. Their transition functions have form $1+\varepsilon f_{ij}$, with imaginary-valued smooth $f_{ij}$ and additive cocycle identity. For a subordinate partition $(\rho_k)$, set $u_i=\sum_k\rho_k f_{ki}$ on chart $i$; terms extend by zero where needed. On an overlap, $u_j-u_i=\sum_k\rho_k(f_{kj}-f_{ki})=f_{ij}$. Changing local frames by $1-\varepsilon u_i$ kills the transitions. A constant unitary infinitesimal scalar then matches the given framing at infinity. Hence every such family can be written globally on the fixed framed line as $d+\varepsilon a$, with $a$ a smooth imaginary-valued one-form; the remaining gauge changes are $1+\varepsilon\phi$ with imaginary-valued $\phi$ and $\phi(\infty)=0$. [F3, F5, step 1.2, construct]

The coefficientwise ASD equation in this global frame is $(da)^+=0$. Write $a=i\alpha$ for a real one-form. Since $d\alpha$ is ASD, $\int|d\alpha|^2=-\int d\alpha\wedge d\alpha=-\int d(\alpha\wedge d\alpha)=0$ by [F4]. Continuity and nonnegativity imply $d\alpha=0$. Again [F4] gives $\alpha=df$; subtract the constant $f(\infty)$ and put $\phi=-if$. The based gauge $1+\varepsilon\phi$ removes $a$. This gauge is unique: a residual imaginary scalar with zero derivative is constant and its value at infinity is zero. Ordinary framed stabilizers were already trivial in step 1.2. The first-order connection groupoid is therefore the trivial point, not merely a set with one known reduced point. [F4, step 2.1, algebra]

A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, algebra]

Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step. [A1, F1, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

boundaries.evidence: 1.1–1.2: positive k raw emptiness conditional on exact rank2 upstream inputs; ordinary U(1) emptiness independently from determinant-flat.
1.2,2.1–5.1: k0 unique framed flat point with actual first-order trivial groupoids.
All steps concern framing rank N=1; no ordinary positive-FI transfer.
4.1: free rank-zero D internal module and U(0) unique; no stabilizer.
k=0 separated from all k>0; S4 infinity included by smooth extension/parallel framing.
AC inherited explicitly; the k0 constant datum/line constructed, no choice made from empty positive-k spaces.
